bull_bear.body:
- Only express logistics operator in India with its own fleet of scheduled Boeing 757-200 and 737 freighter aircraft, offering significant dedicated cargo capacity across the domestic network
- Integrated air and ground network comprising six Boeing 757-200 and two Boeing 737 freighter aircraft, 33,000+ vehicles and 2,492 facilities reaching more than 56,400 locations
- Deep network reach into India's heartland, including Tier II and Tier III markets, enabling capture of emerging-market logistics growth
- Service quality and speed-led reliability, with services monitored to maintain a net service level of 92.1% and a complaint resolution rate of 99.99%
- Membership of DHL Group's DHL eCommerce Solutions division, providing extensive global reach across 220+ countries and territories
- Technology-enabled solutions including 24x7 shipment tracking, dynamic routing, API integrations, real-time courier visibility and route optimisation
- Trusted brand built over more than four decades since operations began in 1983
- Specialised Temperature Controlled Logistics capability for temperature-sensitive healthcare and life sciences shipments
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical disruption to airspace access and trade corridors — MD&A Risks and Concerns (Air Express) states that disruptions affecting airspace access, rerouting around conflict-affected zones and uncertainty across key transport corridors, particularly in light of events in late February and March 2026, have the potential to lengthen flight paths, increase fuel consumption and affect schedule reliability. Blue Dart operates the only scheduled express air network in India, so airspace and corridor shocks hit its core differentiator directly.
- Fuel price and energy market volatility — Flagged in both the air and ground risk sections and by the Chairperson. Volatility in energy markets and pressures on fuel availability influence operating costs and network efficiency; surface logistics networks depend heavily on road transportation and are sensitive to fuel price fluctuations. The Chairperson explicitly names fuel-price volatility among the factors that will continue to test resilience.
- Aviation supply chain dependence and fleet modernisation constraints — The air express sector remains dependent on aircraft manufacturers, engine suppliers, maintenance networks and the timely availability of critical parts. Delays in aircraft deliveries, component shortages and constraints across maintenance and repair ecosystems can restrict cargo capacity, delay fleet modernisation and increase operating costs, limiting the ability to respond to changing demand.
- Intensifying competition and structural shifts in the express logistics ecosystem — Technology-enabled start-ups, asset-light logistics platforms and specialised delivery providers are entering the market with innovative solutions targeting specific segments, creating pricing pressure. Large e-commerce platforms continued to expand their in-house logistics capabilities, influencing shipment flows, and the year pointed to increasing consolidation, with the merger of two industry players underscoring the growing relevance of scale, network density, cost efficiency and technology-led integration.
- Rising operating costs: labour, fleet maintenance and regulatory compliance — Rising operational costs, particularly fuel prices, labour expenses and fleet maintenance costs, together with regulatory changes related to transportation and environmental standards, can affect margins and require continuous optimisation of route planning, fleet utilisation and operational efficiency. Management attributed the FY26 profitability decline in part to an exceptional item related to a new labour code provision and to higher operating expenses and finance costs.
- Cybersecurity and technology resilience — Airlines, cargo operators and logistics platforms depend heavily on digital infrastructure for cargo management, operational control and customer data processing. Alongside cyber threats, aviation authorities have raised concern around operational interference risks in conflict-affected environments including navigation-related disruption, making digital resilience and robust risk controls critical to continuity and to safeguarding data and operations. The Company disclosed one data breach during the year, which it states did not involve customer personally identifiable information and had no material impact.
- Infrastructure variability and last-mile congestion in the ground network — Disparities in road quality, congestion levels and connectivity across regions can still affect transit times and delivery reliability, and these operational challenges are particularly pronounced in last-mile delivery networks where urban congestion and infrastructure limitations impact service efficiency.
- Regulatory fragmentation and rising capital intensity from customer expectations — Diverging regulatory frameworks, evolving tax regimes, trade-related policy shifts and uneven environmental standards across markets increase compliance costs and create friction for operators of global networks, reducing operational efficiency and network flexibility. Separately, meeting rising customer demand for faster, more transparent and more flexible delivery requires investment in real-time tracking, automated sorting facilities and digital logistics platforms, which management notes increases capital expenditure requirements.
- Business concentration: single activity and wholly domestic revenue base — The BRSR discloses that 100% of turnover comes from a single activity, Courier and Express Services (NIC 5320), and that exports contribute Nil to turnover as the Company does not undertake export activities. This makes results wholly dependent on Indian domestic express demand, with no offsetting geographic or activity diversification. Related-party concentration is also high, with 94.47% of loans and advances given to related parties in FY 2025-26.
- Demand volatility and climate/extreme weather exposure — Fluctuations in industrial production, trade activity and consumer demand can lead to uneven shipment volumes, affecting network planning and capacity utilisation. Extreme weather events such as storms, flooding and heatwaves can disrupt airport operations, damage infrastructure and affect flight schedules, while the sector also faces increasing pressure to reduce carbon emissions and transition to sustainable aviation fuel and cleaner technologies, a balance management describes as an important challenge in the years ahead.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The investment case is stated in four blocks: "Market leader in India Express & Parcels Delivery", "Clear strategic direction, investing for growth", "Sustainable growth momentum, unique position for B2B express & eCommerce", and "Enhancing Shareholders Wealth"; elsewhere the deck claims "Dominant market leadership B2B Air Express".
- Key differentiators listed are its own aviation network, market-leading transit times, reliability and high service quality, extensive reach and network, best-in-class technology, strong brand equity, pioneer/innovator status, and "Strong financials and 'Zero Debt' Company".
- Ownership and history: started operations in 1983 by three Indian entrepreneurs, maiden public issue and listing in 1994, DP-DHL acquired Blue Dart in 2005 and currently holds 75% shares; the company is described as an integral part of DHL Group, "world's leading mail and logistics company".
- Business model is explicitly asset-light — "Trucks and facilities are on rentals" — while aviation is owned through wholly owned subsidiaries Blue Dart Aviation Ltd and Concorde Air Logistics Ltd.
- Service history: Ground services launched in 2008 and eCommerce services launched in 2009/2010, giving an integrated air-and-ground pan-India network the deck calls "our key competitive differentiator".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ownership] Shareholding pattern as at June 30, 2026 shows DHL at 75.0%; named holders include HDFC 8.48%, Kotak Mutual Fund 1.86% and Canara Robeco 1.02% among mutual funds, Vanguard 1.0%, iShares 0.55% and Robeco Capital 0.50% among FPIs, and ICICI Pru Life 2.2% and Bajaj Life 0.3% among insurers. The remaining category percentages (3.35%, 11.79%, 2.65%, 2.06%, 5.15%, 2.10%) cannot be bound to their category labels in the extract and are therefore not assigned.
- [Labour Codes] Both the standalone and consolidated performance tables footnote the exceptional item as "Recognition of increased expenses arising from the implementation of the Labour Codes based on it's best judgment during the quarter ended December 31, 2025".
- [Regulation] Structural tailwinds the deck names: Gati Shakti Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity, the National Logistics Policy, Make in India, the eCommerce Policy (which "aims to ensure there are more service providers available... so no monopolies are created"), Open Network for Digital Commerce, dedicated freight corridors and GST-driven centralization of distribution.
- [Macro claims] The deck asserts India is the world's fastest-growing major economy with projected GDP growth of 6.4%-6.8%, a $666.9 billion forex reserve, and multi-decade high credit growth of 17.4%, with resilience despite West Asian energy shocks.
- [Margin trend, basis unstated] The track-record chart labels EBDITA Margin as 2020-21 11.0%, 2021-22 15.7%, 2022-23 13.1%, 2023-24 11.0%, 2024-25 9.9% and 2025-26 9.7%. This 9.7% for FY2025-26 matches neither the standalone (10.44%) nor the consolidated (16.05%) FY2025-26 EBITDA margin printed in the same deck's quarter-wise tables, and the deck does not reconcile the two.

business.body: Blue Dart provides premium express logistics in India, ranging from the delivery of a single document to large shipment consignments, across the air express segment, the ground express segment and multimodal express solutions on day-definite and time-definite delivery schedules. It is the only express logistics operator in India with its own fleet of scheduled Boeing 757-200 and 737 freighter aircraft, supported by bonded warehouses, ground handling and maintenance capabilities. As part of DHL Group's DHL eCommerce Solutions division, it serves large enterprises, MSMEs, e-commerce players, healthcare and life sciences companies, banking and financial services institutions, manufacturers and individual shippers, with international connectivity across 220+ countries and territories.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Enhance network productivity and strengthen the operational backbone through investments in infrastructure, technology, automation and network capacity.
- Accelerate digital transformation: simplify customer journeys, improve shipment visibility, enable faster decision-making and strengthen network responsiveness, alongside data governance, cybersecurity, responsible deployment and workforce readiness.
- Advance sustainable logistics solutions, aligned with DHL Group's Strategy 2030 'Accelerate Sustainable Growth', integrating environmental responsibility into operations and investment decisions.
- Deepen customer engagement across emerging markets and high-growth regions and sectors, including e-commerce, healthcare and MSMEs.
- Focus on innovation, reach expansion, improvements in transit time, activation of emerging towns (Tier II, III and IV) and strengthening distribution channels to enhance reach.
- Further strengthen and consolidate the air and ground infrastructure.
- Maintain execution discipline, service reliability and resilience across the value chain, aligning priorities to evolving customer needs and demand patterns.
- Drive the 'First Choice' and 'Net Promoter Approach' (NPA) initiatives to enhance process improvements, customer centricity and service quality.
- Continue investing in the digital capabilities of the workforce so that technology translates into measurable business value and consistent service delivery.
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation and cost management while investing in capacity, technology and service quality.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Blue Dart's expansion during FY 2025-26 was network- and infrastructure-led rather than plant-based. The flagship milestone was the inauguration of its largest Green Integrated Ground Hub at Pataudi, Haryana (also described as the North Integrated Ground Hub), strengthening nationwide connectivity, automation and sustainable logistics capabilities; the facility was strategically designed to enhance throughput and operational efficiency, improve line-haul connectivity, processing efficiency and overall network resilience, and integrates sustainability considerations into its design and operations. The Company operates 2,492 facilities / hubs / offices across India and, through its wholly owned subsidiary Blue Dart Aviation Ltd., a fleet of six Boeing 757-200 and two Boeing 737 freighter aircraft with a payload capacity of over 500 tonnes per night, supported by more than 33,000 vehicles and 599 electric vehicles serving 19,000+ pin codes. Digital build-out during the year included the Digital Account Opening (DAO) platform, integrated with the Digital Prepaid Card framework, enabling businesses to onboard and start shipping within 10 minutes. Looking forward, the Company states it plans to further strengthen and consolidate its air and ground infrastructure and expand its reach, and continues to focus on reach expansion, improvements in transit time, activation of emerging towns (Tier II, III and IV) and strengthening distribution channels. Sustainability-linked fleet expansion continues via the electric vehicle base, which reached 599 vehicles as of March 2026, and the stated focus on transitioning to more fuel-efficient aircraft. No rupee capex quantum is usably disclosed: the only capital-commitments block supplied carries no attributable period and no printed unit. The BRSR Principle 2 disclosure states that R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were Nil in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, as the nature of the Company's operations does not require them.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Stable domestic demand, continued formalisation of supply chains and increasing adoption of organised logistics solutions supported performance; shipment momentum was driven by SMEs, sustained traction across e-commerce, B2B surface express, and both B2B and B2C product segments.
- Rising logistics activity across Tier II and Tier III markets, which management says continued to play an important role in India's logistics growth story and which Blue Dart's extensive network enabled it to capture.
- As businesses increasingly adopt integrated supply chain systems and digital logistics platforms, the demand for reliable express transportation and distribution services is expected to grow steadily.
- The outlook for India's logistics sector remains robust, supported by rising consumption, expanding digital commerce, infrastructure development, manufacturing growth and continued supply-chain formalisation.
- Counter-drivers management flags: geopolitical uncertainty, fuel-price volatility, technological disruption and intensifying competition will continue to test the resilience of businesses.
- Government policy tailwinds: the National Logistics Policy and PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, Union Budget 2026 infrastructure allocation, exemption of customs duty on aviation components, and removal of the Rs 10 lakh per consignment value cap on courier exports, which is expected to strengthen cross-border e-commerce for MSMEs and D2C brands.
- Indian logistics market is estimated at USD 317 billion to USD 380 billion with logistics costs at 9%-11% of GDP; India's express logistics segment is estimated at approximately USD 9 billion in FY2025.
- Margin context stated by management: FY26 profitability declined marginally, attributable to an exceptional item related to a new labour code provision and to higher operating expenses and finance costs in relation to network expansion and inflationary pressures.
- Expansion of e-commerce, increasing complexity of global trade networks and rising demand for integrated logistics solutions are expected to sustain long-term growth in the global logistics sector.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Blue Dart delivered steady 7-8% revenue growth in FY26 driven by ground e-commerce volumes, but Q4 margins compressed 17% YoY due to unfavorable mix shift toward heavier/ground freight and one-off labor code costs. While top-line momentum persists, profitability recovery hinges on optimizing the lower-yield ground segment and managing recurring high maintenance capex.

currentContext.expansion: Blue Dart's expansion during FY 2025-26 was network- and infrastructure-led rather than plant-based. The flagship milestone was the inauguration of its largest Green Integrated Ground Hub at Pataudi, Haryana (also described as the North Integrated Ground Hub), strengthening nationwide connectivity, automation and sustainable logistics capabilities; the facility was strategically designed to enhance throughput and operational efficiency, improve line-haul connectivity, processing efficiency and overall network resilience, and integrates sustainability considerations into its design and operations. The Company operates 2,492 facilities / hubs / offices across India and, through its wholly owned subsidiary Blue Dart Aviation Ltd., a fleet of six Boeing 757-200 and two Boeing 737 freighter aircraft with a payload capacity of over 500 tonnes per night, supported by more than 33,000 vehicles and 599 electric vehicles serving 19,000+ pin codes. Digital build-out during the year included the Digital Account Opening (DAO) platform, integrated with the Digital Prepaid Card framework, enabling businesses to onboard and start shipping within 10 minutes. Looking forward, the Company states it plans to further strengthen and consolidate its air and ground infrastructure and expand its reach, and continues to focus on reach expansion, improvements in transit time, activation of emerging towns (Tier II, III and IV) and strengthening distribution channels. Sustainability-linked fleet expansion continues via the electric vehicle base, which reached 599 vehicles as of March 2026, and the stated focus on transitioning to more fuel-efficient aircraft. No rupee capex quantum is usably disclosed: the only capital-commitments block supplied carries no attributable period and no printed unit. The BRSR Principle 2 disclosure states that R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were Nil in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, as the nature of the Company's operations does not require them.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to airspace access and trade corridors
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns (Air Express) states that disruptions affecting airspace access, rerouting around conflict-affected zones and uncertainty across key transport corridors, particularly in light of events in late February and March 2026, have the potential to lengthen flight paths, increase fuel consumption and affect schedule reliability. Blue Dart operates the only scheduled express air network in India, so airspace and corridor shocks hit its core differentiator directly.

risks.risk: Fuel price and energy market volatility
risks.note: Flagged in both the air and ground risk sections and by the Chairperson. Volatility in energy markets and pressures on fuel availability influence operating costs and network efficiency; surface logistics networks depend heavily on road transportation and are sensitive to fuel price fluctuations. The Chairperson explicitly names fuel-price volatility among the factors that will continue to test resilience.

risks.risk: Aviation supply chain dependence and fleet modernisation constraints
risks.note: The air express sector remains dependent on aircraft manufacturers, engine suppliers, maintenance networks and the timely availability of critical parts. Delays in aircraft deliveries, component shortages and constraints across maintenance and repair ecosystems can restrict cargo capacity, delay fleet modernisation and increase operating costs, limiting the ability to respond to changing demand.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition and structural shifts in the express logistics ecosystem
risks.note: Technology-enabled start-ups, asset-light logistics platforms and specialised delivery providers are entering the market with innovative solutions targeting specific segments, creating pricing pressure. Large e-commerce platforms continued to expand their in-house logistics capabilities, influencing shipment flows, and the year pointed to increasing consolidation, with the merger of two industry players underscoring the growing relevance of scale, network density, cost efficiency and technology-led integration.

risks.risk: Rising operating costs: labour, fleet maintenance and regulatory compliance
risks.note: Rising operational costs, particularly fuel prices, labour expenses and fleet maintenance costs, together with regulatory changes related to transportation and environmental standards, can affect margins and require continuous optimisation of route planning, fleet utilisation and operational efficiency. Management attributed the FY26 profitability decline in part to an exceptional item related to a new labour code provision and to higher operating expenses and finance costs.

Airlines, cargo operators and logistics platforms depend heavily on digital infrastructure for cargo management, operational control and customer data processing. Alongside cyber threats, aviation authorities have raised concern around operational interference risks in conflict-affected environments including navigation-related disruption, making digital resilience and robust risk controls critical to continuity and to safeguarding data and operations. The Company disclosed one data breach during the year, which it states did not involve customer personally identifiable information and had no material impact.

risks.risk: Infrastructure variability and last-mile congestion in the ground network
risks.note: Disparities in road quality, congestion levels and connectivity across regions can still affect transit times and delivery reliability, and these operational challenges are particularly pronounced in last-mile delivery networks where urban congestion and infrastructure limitations impact service efficiency.

risks.risk: Regulatory fragmentation and rising capital intensity from customer expectations
risks.note: Diverging regulatory frameworks, evolving tax regimes, trade-related policy shifts and uneven environmental standards across markets increase compliance costs and create friction for operators of global networks, reducing operational efficiency and network flexibility. Separately, meeting rising customer demand for faster, more transparent and more flexible delivery requires investment in real-time tracking, automated sorting facilities and digital logistics platforms, which management notes increases capital expenditure requirements.

risks.risk: Business concentration: single activity and wholly domestic revenue base
risks.note: The BRSR discloses that 100% of turnover comes from a single activity, Courier and Express Services (NIC 5320), and that exports contribute Nil to turnover as the Company does not undertake export activities. This makes results wholly dependent on Indian domestic express demand, with no offsetting geographic or activity diversification. Related-party concentration is also high, with 94.47% of loans and advances given to related parties in FY 2025-26.

risks.risk: Demand volatility and climate/extreme weather exposure
risks.note: Fluctuations in industrial production, trade activity and consumer demand can lead to uneven shipment volumes, affecting network planning and capacity utilisation. Extreme weather events such as storms, flooding and heatwaves can disrupt airport operations, damage infrastructure and affect flight schedules, while the sector also faces increasing pressure to reduce carbon emissions and transition to sustainable aviation fuel and cleaner technologies, a balance management describes as an important challenge in the years ahead.

one-line thesis: Blue Dart delivered steady 7-8% revenue growth in FY26 driven by ground e-commerce volumes, but Q4 margins compressed 17% YoY due to unfavorable mix shift toward heavier/ground freight and one-off labor code costs. While top-line momentum persists, profitability recovery hinges on optimizing the lower-yield ground segment and managing recurring high maintenance capex.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 6,141cr FY26 (+7% YoY), INR 1,533cr Q4 (+8% YoY); EBITDA Margin: Compressed in Q4 (PBT -17% YoY pre-exceptionals) due to mix/costs; PAT: INR 240cr FY26, INR 43cr Q4; Order Book: N/A (Spot market); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but high ROU assets for leases; One-offs: Labor Code implementation costs impacted full year PBT, Q4 saw INR 10-15cr timing costs (vehicle hiring, staff).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Only express logistics operator in India with its own fleet of scheduled Boeing 757-200 and 737 freighter aircraft, offering significant dedicated cargo capacity across the domestic network
- Integrated air and ground network comprising six Boeing 757-200 and two Boeing 737 freighter aircraft, 33,000+ vehicles and 2,492 facilities reaching more than 56,400 locations
- Deep network reach into India's heartland, including Tier II and Tier III markets, enabling capture of emerging-market logistics growth
- Service quality and speed-led reliability, with services monitored to maintain a net service level of 92.1% and a complaint resolution rate of 99.99%
- Membership of DHL Group's DHL eCommerce Solutions division, providing extensive global reach across 220+ countries and territories
- Technology-enabled solutions including 24x7 shipment tracking, dynamic routing, API integrations, real-time courier visibility and route optimisation
- Trusted brand built over more than four decades since operations began in 1983
- Specialised Temperature Controlled Logistics capability for temperature-sensitive healthcare and life sciences shipments

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Continued mix shift to low-yield ground freight; Labor cost inflation from new codes; Fuel price volatility if surcharge lag increases; Competition from asset-light aggregators in B2C.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Aircraft maintenance (INR 200cr) is booked as Capex but is effectively recurring Opex equivalent; Ground expansion yields lower incremental ROI than air due to variable cost structure; B2C is almost entirely e-commerce with minimal large platform dependency (fragmented D2C/aggregators).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Enhance network productivity and strengthen the operational backbone through investments in infrastructure, technology, automation and network capacity.
- Accelerate digital transformation: simplify customer journeys, improve shipment visibility, enable faster decision-making and strengthen network responsiveness, alongside data governance, cybersecurity, responsible deployment and workforce readiness.
- Advance sustainable logistics solutions, aligned with DHL Group's Strategy 2030 'Accelerate Sustainable Growth', integrating environmental responsibility into operations and investment …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Ownership] Shareholding pattern as at June 30, 2026 shows DHL at 75.0%; named holders include HDFC 8.48%, Kotak Mutual Fund 1.86% and Canara Robeco 1.02% among mutual funds, Vanguard 1.0%, iShares 0.55% and Robeco Capital 0.50% among FPIs, and ICICI Pru Life 2.2% and Bajaj Life 0.3% among insurers. The remaining category percentages (3.35%, 11.79%, 2.65%, 2.06%, 5.15%, 2.10%) cannot be bound to their category labels in the extract and are therefore not assigned.
- [Labour Codes] Both the standalone and consolidated performance tables footnote the exceptional item as "Recognition of increased expenses arising from the implementation of the Labour Codes based on it's best judgment during the quarter ended December 31, 2025".
- [Regulation] Structural tailwinds the deck names: Gati Shakti Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity, the National Logistics Policy, Make in India, the eCommerce Policy (which "aims to ensure there are more service providers available... so no monopolies are created"), Open Network for Digital Commerce, dedicated freight corridors and GST-driven centralization of distribution.
- [Macro claims] The deck asserts India is the world's fastest-growing major economy with projected GDP growth of 6.4%-6.8%, a $666.9 billion forex reserve, and multi-decade high credit growth of 17.4%, with resilience despite West Asian energy shocks.
- [Margin trend, basis unstated] The track-record chart labels EBDITA Margin as 2020-21 11.0%, 2021-22 15.7%, 2022-23 13.1%, 2023-24 11.0%, 2024-25 9.9% and 2025-26 9.7%. This 9.7% for FY2025-26 matches neither the standalone (10.44%) nor the consolidated (16.05%) FY2025-26 EBITDA margin printed in the same deck's quarter-wise tables, and the deck does not reconcile the two.

one-line thesis: Blue Dart delivered steady 7-8% revenue growth in FY26 driven by ground e-commerce volumes, but Q4 margins compressed 17% YoY due to unfavorable mix shift toward heavier/ground freight and one-off labor code costs. While top-line momentum persists, profitability recovery hinges on optimizing the lower-yield ground segment and managing recurring high maintenance capex.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 6,141cr FY26 (+7% YoY), INR 1,533cr Q4 (+8% YoY); EBITDA Margin: Compressed in Q4 (PBT -17% YoY pre-exceptionals) due to mix/costs; PAT: INR 240cr FY26, INR 43cr Q4; Order Book: N/A (Spot market); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but high ROU assets for leases; One-offs: Labor Code implementation costs impacted full year PBT, Q4 saw INR 10-15cr timing costs (vehicle hiring, staff).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Steady organic growth aligned with GDP/e-commerce; Margin: Targeting 7-8% PBT margin (currently lagging); Order Inflow: Balanced growth between Air (8.8% vol) and Ground (6.9% vol); Capex: Recurring INR 250-270cr annually (INR 100-150cr aircraft maintenance + INR 120cr ground/IT).
order book & pipeline: N/A - Transactional spot business; Volume visibility driven by e-commerce contracts and B2B retainers.
segment / subsidiary detail: Revenue Mix: Air 60%, Ground 40% (Ground share rising); Customer Mix: B2B 70%, B2C 30% (B2C is pure e-commerce); E-commerce split: 17% Air, 12% Surface of total revenue; Volume Growth FY26: Air +8.8%, Ground +6.9%; Tonnage FY26: ~1.44M tons (+7.1%).
growth verticals / optionality: Ground network expansion remains primary engine; Automation/sorters in hubs to improve handling efficiency; Limited international charter upside currently.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin pressure from mix shift to heavier ground freight (lower yield/kg); Labor Code wage hikes; Local vehicle hiring costs spiked in March; Fuel volatility neutralized via surcharges (Brent/ATF link).
capex / expansion: FY26 Total: INR 360cr (Consol); Breakup: INR 200cr Aircraft Maintenance (C/D checks - recurring), INR 120cr Standalone (Ground hubs, IT, Sorters); Future: ~INR 150cr/yr aircraft maint + ~INR 120cr/yr ground/IT renewal.
capital allocation: Focus on sustaining network reliability; No major new fleet acquisition; Lease-heavy model for ground facilities (ROU assets); Dividend policy not discussed in detail but implied stable.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
